# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This is a practical guide to dose-response meta-analysis: pooling studies not to
ask whether an exposure matters, but to ask how the effect changes as the dose
changes.

Most meta-analysis teaching stops at a single pooled estimate. That estimate
answers "treated versus untreated" and nothing else. It cannot tell you whether
twice the dose buys twice the benefit, whether benefit stops accruing past some
point, or whether more becomes worse. Those are dose-response questions, and
they need a different model.

## Who this is for {.unnumbered .no-slide}

You have run a meta-analysis before, or at least watched one being run. You know
what a forest plot is and what heterogeneity means. You do not need to know any
dose-response methods: that is what this book is for.

Code is in R. Every analysis uses `dosresmeta` [@dosresmeta], with the companion
package `easyDR` for the checks that come before and after the model.

## How this book is organised {.unnumbered .no-slide}

Five chapters, in the order you would actually do the work:

| Chapter | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| 1 | What is a dose-response meta-analysis, and should you run one? |
| 2 | Can your studies support one, and how do you extract the data? |
| 3 | How do you register it, and how do you rate the studies? |
| 4 | What is the model doing, and how do you run it? |
| 5 | How do you check it, write it up and read it honestly? |

Each chapter is the written half of a class. The chapters and the videos follow
the same five steps, in the same order, so they can be used together or apart.

## Conventions {.unnumbered .no-slide}

Runnable code appears in blocks you can copy:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(easyDR)
easydr(my_data, sm = "RR", shape = "linear")
```
:::


Terms are defined where they first matter rather than in a glossary, because a
definition you meet in use is a definition you keep.

::: {.cta}
**This chapter is the written half of a class.** The [Meta-Analysis
Academy](https://metahub.metaanalysisacademy.com) course walks through the same
material on video, with the worked example built live, the templates ready to
fill, and somewhere to ask when your data does not look like the example.

Found an error, or something explained badly? [Open an
issue](https://github.com/vanioljantunes/easyDR/issues) — corrections are
welcome and credited.
:::
